title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: LUIS'S TICKETS
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Luis Ortega, a parking officer in Milwaukee, Wisconsin.
He wrote tickets for a living. So you can guess how popular he was.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE YELLING
segments.quote: Men are disturbed not by things, but by the view which they take of them.
segments.author: Epictetus
lines: Every day, somebody yelled at Luis. One man called him a vampire with a printer.
His wife Ana read him a line from Epictetus, an old Greek thinker:
Men are disturbed not by things, but by the view which they take of them.
Luis got it. They were mad at the ticket, not at him. So he stopped arguing, and started saying good morning.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE BROKEN METER
segments.quote: Change happens by listening and then starting a dialogue with the people who are doing something you don't believe is right.
segments.author: Jane Goodall
lines: Then a barber named Walt ran out of his shop, red in the face.
Luis wanted to shout back. But he remembered words from Jane Goodall, the famous chimp scientist:
Change happens by listening and then starting a dialogue with the people who are doing something you don't believe is right.
So he listened. Walt had paid. The meter was broken. Luis helped him fight the ticket, and Walt won.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE BREAK ROOM
segments.quote: Any fool can criticize, condemn and complain - and most fools do.
segments.author: Dale Carnegie
lines: At the office, the other officers loved to complain. The drivers, the boss, the coffee.
Then Luis found an old Dale Carnegie book in the lost and found:
Any fool can criticize, condemn and complain, and most fools do.
Luis shut the book. Maybe people got tickets because nobody ever explained the rules.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE MAP
segments.quote: Preparation, I have often said, is rightly two-thirds of any venture.
segments.author: Amelia Earhart
lines: So he planned a little card, with every free parking spot and street cleaning day.
He wanted to rush it. But Ana's fridge magnet had words from Amelia Earhart, the famous pilot:
Preparation, I have often said, is rightly two-thirds of any venture.
So he checked every sign for three weeks. Then he handed out five hundred cards. Tickets on his route dropped by half.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE ROOKIES
segments.author: Seneca
lines: His boss noticed, and asked him to train the new officers. Luis was terrified. He had never taught anything except his dog, and the dog still does not sit.
His uncle Ray sent him a line from Seneca, the Roman thinker:
While we teach, we learn.
And he did. The rookies asked smart questions, and the cards got even better.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE SANDWICH
segments.quote: Accomplishment is something you cannot buy.
segments.author: Roberto Clemente
lines: A year later, Brady Street threw Luis a party on the sidewalk. The diner named a sandwich after him. It comes with a warning.
Walt, the only Pittsburgh Pirates fan in Milwaukee, raised his coffee and quoted Roberto Clemente:
Accomplishment is something you cannot buy.
Luis never got a raise. But that day, he felt like the richest man on the street.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Choose your view. Listen first. Stop complaining. Prepare well. Teach. Earn what money can't buy.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Choose how you see it. Listen first. Stop complaining. Prepare well. Teach what you know. And earn what money can't buy.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night. And please, feed the meter.
